formula: E = m · c²   avec  c = 3·10⁸ m/s
sketch:
Observe: SVG display of Einstein's E = mc² with 3 interactive
fields — m (in kg or u), Δm (mass defect in u), and computed E
(in J or MeV). Student edits any two, third computes; unit
converters (1 u = 931.5 MeV/c²) surface prominently. A "conservation
ledger" panel shows before/after masses for a chosen nuclear
reaction, revealing the Δm that becomes energy. Experiment: 3
seeded (reaction, target E) tuples; student computes Δm. Evaluate:
unit-converter helper hidden; student enters E in MeV from raw Δm
in u using the constant from memory.
